Each pushed character takes one physical stress. Using this effect also pushes around anything else that happens to be in your zone.

entities.name: Deflection
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you are aware of a projectile attack against you, you can generate a shield at a precise angle, redirecting the attack to any other target in your zone or an adjacent zone. The new target defends against the attack. Doing this makes your shield break apart, however, throwing shards of invisible force all around your environment.

entities.name: Master Slowing
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You have perfected your ability to hold people in place. Gain +2 to Shoot when slowing targets.

entities.name: Slow Field
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can affect an entire zone with your power. Select a zone up to one zone away, and roll Shoot with a -2 penalty. Your power affects every target in the zone, friend and foe.

entities.name: Stop
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

When you entangle your opponents, you entangle them completely. When slowing a target, you may choose to roll Shoot with a -2 penalty. If you do, your target cannot take any physical actions until they escape from your power.

entities.name: Mass Slowing
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

When pressed, you can apply your slowing effect on a massive scale, targeting everyone in your zone and every adjacent zone. Of course, by affecting so many targets, you’re likely to damage something in the environment as well.

entities.name: Timeless Zone
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your power comes from an ability to manipulate time itself. You can turn your zone into a bubble of stopped time; nobody and nothing—not even you—can enter or pass through it, and nobody within it can take any actions, until you release the effect or the scene ends. However, the border between regular and timeless space is a strange and dangerous thing, which will kick up powerful winds and potentially destroy whatever gets too close.

entities.name: Basic Super Agility
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You are preternaturally graceful, and gain +2 to Athletics when leaping, balancing, or otherwise demonstrating your agility. In addition, you have a prodigious leap: leaping up to a second-story window or from rooftop to rooftop across a wide alleyway is a simple task that, without further complication, requires no Athletics roll.

entities.name: Master Super Agility
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain an additional +2 bonus to Athletics when demonstrating your superior agility.

entities.name: Uncanny Dodge
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you can see a projectile coming, you can get out of its way with some clever gymnastics. You gain +2 to defense rolls when dodging ranged attacks.

entities.name: Mighty Bound
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you put everything you have into it, you can leap incredible distances, from the ground to basically any outdoor point in the city. Of course, putting that much muscle into a jump will crack the pavement, both where you jump from and where you land.

entities.name: Hair-Trigger Reaction
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you are targeted by a ranged attack from another zone, you can use your superhuman agility to not just leap out of the way, but also leap toward your attacker, landing in their zone. This causes the attack to miss you, but it will still hit something in your zone.

entities.name: Basic Super Intelligence
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain +2 to Will when working though puzzles, riddles, or other mentally absorbing tasks. In addition, you can answer complicated mathematical problems instantly.

entities.name: Master Super Intelligence
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain an additional +2 to Will when demonstrating your mental acuity.

entities.name: Walking Library
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You’ve forgotten more than most people will ever know. By spending a fate point, you can use Will in place of Lore and gain the bonus to Will from Super Intelligence, even if it’s not a mentally absorbing task.

entities.name: Chessmastery
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You don’t just understand facts; you understand how people operate. You gain +2 to Empathy when attempting to predict someone’s future actions.

entities.name: Taskmastery
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Once you see how someone fights, you can exploit their weaknesses. When someone deals physical stress to you in a conflict, you gain +2 to all attack rolls against them until the end of the scene.

entities.name: Precognition
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your intelligence is so far beyond the norm that you can predict the near-future with uncanny accuracy.

entities.name: Pawn Interception
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use your gift for analysis to divert an incoming attack. When an attack would hit you, you can have it instead strike a nameless NPC in your zone—they just happened to wander into the line of fire at the exact right moment. When this happens, you take no damage and the NPC is taken out.

entities.name: Battle Plan
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your tactical mind has figured out exactly how a given conflict will shape up—you just need to remind your companions what to do. You can shout out a battle plan to give yourself and every ally in the scene the boost We’ve Planned for This. Unfortunately, doing so will give whomever you’re fighting a little insight into your tactics.

entities.name: Basic Super Senses
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Pick a single sense—sight, hearing, smell, taste, or touch. You gain +2 to Investigate when using that sense. In addition, that sense cannot be impeded; for instance, you can see in darkness or hear clearly in a cacophony.

entities.name: Master Super Senses
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain an additional +2 to Investigate when using your superior sense.

entities.name: Alertness
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your senses are heightened even when you aren’t really trying. You gain +2 to Notice against anything you could identify with your superior sense.

entities.name: Mental Map
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your senses are so finely tuned that you can create a full mental map of an entire floor of a building in an instant; all you need to do is clap your hands and listen to the echoes, or perhaps light a fire and watch the way the air currents move the smoke. Whatever the method, it gets you the layout of the building, but it’ll likely attract unwanted attention.

entities.name: Hyperfocus
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can focus the full power of your super sense on someone anywhere in the scene. Because of your superior focus, you gain +4 to all attack and defense rolls against your target until you end this effect or the target is taken out. However, you cannot attack anyone else while hyperfocused, and you are liable to cause collateral damage because you’ve stopped paying attention to your surroundings.

entities.name: Basic Super Speed
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain +2 to Athletics rolls that involve moving quickly. Additionally, you can move quickly enough to run across liquids or up sheer vertical surfaces—although if you slow down or stop, you’ll fall.

entities.name: Master Super Speed
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You are faster than fast! Gain an additional +2 bonus to Athletics when moving quickly.

entities.name: Improved Reaction Time
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use Athletics in place of any other skill for the purpose of determining turn order.

entities.name: Phasing
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

By concentrating carefully, you can accelerate the molecules in your body to such a point that they no longer interact with common, unaccelerated matter.

entities.name: Lots of Actions
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can split your shifts among up to three different actions, adding +1 to each.

entities.name: Quantum Tunneling
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If pressed, you can run fast enough to break through time itself. You and anyone and anything you are holding onto disappear completely, reappearing in the same position in the future—as little as one exchange later, but up to a week, with no time having passed for you. The spontaneous return to the natural flow of time, however, is sudden and potentially violent.

entities.name: Speed Demon
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you’re willing to tear up the streets—shattering glass, injuring pedestrians, and such—you can travel pretty much anywhere in the same city in the span of a single exchange.

entities.name: Basic Super Strength
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain +2 to Physique in all situations that require pure strength.

entities.name: Master Super Strength
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

There’s strong, and then there’s you. Gain an additional +2 bonus to Physique in situations requiring pure strength.

entities.name: Hammer Toss
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can move a target of your attack up to four zones away.

entities.name: Basic Super Toughness
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain Armor:2 against any purely physical damage.

entities.name: Master Super Toughness
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Pain don’t hurt. You gain an additional physical stress box.

entities.name: Implacable
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

The best defense it not even noticing that someone is attacking you. You gain Armor:4 against physical damage.

entities.name: Juggernaut
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Running around obstacles is for people afraid of running through them. You gain +2 to any attempt to overcome an obstacle impeding your movement by smashing right through it.

entities.name: Shrug It Off
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You immediately heal a mild consequence.

entities.name: Bulletproof
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can, at will, shrug off any amount of physical stress from a single source—bullets simply bounce off your chest, uselessly. However, the damage is reflected into your environment; bullets gotta go somewhere, after all.

entities.name: Interception
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

When someone, up to one zone away, is attacked, you can intervene, throwing yourself in front of them to defend for them. Leaping into action and throwing targets out of the way, however, will incur its own damage. All this assumes you are able to move there, of course.

entities.name: Basic Telekinesis
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can move small objects in your own or adjacent zones without physically touching them. By hurling objects around, you can attack with Will against targets in your zone.

entities.name: Master Telekinesis
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain +2 to Will when attacking with telekinesis.

entities.name: Long-Distance Telekinesis
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your mental abilities stretch unusually far. You can move objects and make attacks up to three zones away using telekinesis.

entities.name: Telekinetic Might
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use Will to lift large objects. Lifting something human-sized is a Fair (+2) obstacle, while a car is a Great (+4) obstacle.

entities.name: TK Shield
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can ward off physical attacks with the power of your mind. By erecting a telekinetic shield, you can defend with Will against physical attacks.

entities.name: Super Strength
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

By working your muscles and mind in tandem, you can deliver more power than either on its own, effectively giving you super strength.

entities.name: Holding Pattern
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

By pouring everything you have into your telekinetic power, you can lift everyone and everything in your zone and adjacent zones off the ground. Lifted targets cannot move or take physical actions that require movement, such as using Fight, but they can still use Shoot or mental attacks.

entities.name: Unstoppable Telekinesis
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use your mental powers to lift something up to the size of a tank and hurl it, either to destroy a wall or similarly robust obstacle, or to attack every target in your zone or an adjacent zone.

entities.name: Basic Telepathy
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Choose one skill from Empathy, Investigate, or Notice. You can use this skill to glean information from the minds of people in your zone or adjacent zones. If your target knows or suspects you are reading their mind, they can actively oppose you with Will. Empathy can discover what someone is feeling, Investigate delves into deep thoughts and memories, and Notice picks up surface thoughts and detects unfamiliar minds. You can also project words into the minds of anyone within range.

entities.name: Master Telepathy
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You are a skilled mind reader. You gain +2 to your telepathic skills when reading minds.

entities.name: Long-Distance Telepathy
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can read the minds of others regardless of distance, so long as you can see them.

entities.name: Mental Blasts
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use Will to launch mental attacks up to three zones away. If you take out someone with such an attack, you can either render them comatose or take control of their mind.

entities.name: Telepathic Flexilbility
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You know many ways to read a mind. Choose another skill you can use to read minds.

entities.name: Influence
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Not only can you read minds, but you can also tweak them. Just a little. Just to your advantage.

entities.name: Psychic Lockdown
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can mentally overwhelm everyone else in the scene, effectively freezing them. They can’t take physical actions, but they can still invoke aspects and perform mental tasks. They can attempt to break out by overcoming with Will, opposed by your Will. On each of your turns, you must concentrate, using your action, to keep them frozen. The psychic brain-lock will definitely have lasting effects on their brains.

entities.name: Basic Teleportation
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can move up to three zones as an action, provided that you can see where you are moving to.

entities.name: Teleportation Mastery
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can move an additional zone when you teleport.

entities.name: Collective Teleportation
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Normally you can only teleport yourself, but with a little effort you can teleport any human-sized target you touch. If the target resists, make an attack using Fight to grab them against their will.

entities.name: Mark and Recall
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

By concentrating for a few minutes in a location, you can mark it. Thereafter, you can always teleport back to your marked location, regardless of distance. You may change your marked location whenever you want, but you can only have one marked location at a time.

entities.name: Item Summoning
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Back home you’ve got a big collection of useful things, which you can teleport into your hands whenever you need to.

entities.name: Wormhole
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can chain together two zones with a slightly unstable wormhole, tearing reality as you know it into little bits. Pick any two zones you can see; these zones are considered the same zone for all purposes.

entities.name: Jaunt
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can teleport to any location in the city that you have seen before, even if just in photos. Unfortunately, this imprecise maneuver usually ends with you crashing through something important.

entities.name: Basic Wall-Crawling
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can move along any solid surface, even upside-down, as easily as you move along the ground. In addition, you get +2 to Athletics while navigating obstacles that involve climbing.

entities.name: Master Wall-Crawling
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain an additional +2 bonus to Athletics when climbing.

entities.name: Wall Kick
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can leap off the wall to put a little more punch into your punches. You gain +2 to Fight if you can attack someone by jumping off a wall.

entities.name: Tireless Grip
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

If you find a comfortable spot on a wall or ceiling, you can hang there for hours if need be. You can even sleep there perfectly safely.

entities.name: Gravity Manipulation
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your wall-crawling ability actually comes from your ability to adjust the pull of gravity on yourself so that “down” is where you want it to be, at least for a few minutes. You can expand this gravity trick to cover an entire zone, pulling everyone and everything not nailed down into the wall you’re standing on. Anyone who hasn’t braced for impact must overcome a Fair (+2) obstacle using Athletics; otherwise, they land poorly and take a mild consequence.

entities.name: Hold Fast
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can bring any moving object, up to the size and speed of a train, to a complete halt, provided you can hold onto it with one hand and onto something reasonably solid, like the ground, with the other. Doing this doesn’t hurt you—your body is built to handle these forces—but it will probably damage whatever you’re trying to stop.

entities.name: Basic Weather Control
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can fill your zone with specific weather patterns by creating an advantage using Will. The opposition is generally Fair (+2), but increases with especially difficult weather, such as tornadoes, or especially inclement weather, such as snow during high summer. These weather patterns fade away when you will them to, when you leave the zone, or otherwise at the end of the scene.

entities.name: Master Weather Control
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You gain +2 to Will when creating a weather pattern.

entities.name: Weather Precision
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use Will to attack any target in a zone in which you’ve created a weather pattern.

entities.name: Lingering Weather
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Weather patterns you create linger while you are in an adjacent zone. In addition, you can create weather patterns in adjacent zones.

entities.name: Dangerous Weather
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your weather pattern makes a Great (+4) attack against a single target in its zone.

entities.name: Horrifying to Behold
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Something about your appearance is so unsettling that it actually hurts people to get close to you. Anyone who attacks you using Fight takes a mild mental consequence if they don’t already have one.

entities.name: Ongoing Mutations
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Once per scene, you can spend a fate point to undergo a dramatic sudden mutation. This lets you to switch the ranks of any two skills of adjacent rank.

entities.name: Obvious Target
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You don’t need to work hard to get someone to want you dead. You gain +2 to Provoke when attempting to make a target attack or follow you.

entities.name: Decay
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use your corruption to accelerate the natural decay of virtually everything in your zone. Living targets have some resistance and only take 2 physical stress, while inanimate targets are more adversely affected—virtually everything, including the walls and the floor, withers to dust.

entities.name: Power Generation
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can power any electrical device just by holding it. If you put your fingers to an electrical outlet, you can provide power for an entire apartment.

entities.name: Conductive Trip
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can briefly convert your entire body into electricity and push through conductive material. You can use this power to pass through an otherwise impenetrable barrier, such as a door with a metal doorknob, as an action.

entities.name: Through the Grid
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can leap into any electrical outlet in the city and emerge a moment later from another one, provided you have a general idea where it is and you are willing to short out and overload electronics at your destination.

entities.name: Friend to Flames
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You cannot be harmed by fire of any sort, whether you generated it with your power or not.

entities.name: Fire Control
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

In addition to generating fire, you can manipulate it, causing flames to spread where you want them to. Getting flames to spread in a specific direction requires you to overcome a Fair (+2) obstacle with Provoke; more complex fire maneuvers increase that opposition.

entities.name: Flame On
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You light yourself on fire. It’s GREAT. You gain the situation aspect On Fire with one free invoke. If you are already On Fire, gain another free invoke and clear your highest marked physical stress box.

entities.name: Flaming
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can surround yourself in flames that burn everything and everyone. Fires start near you, and anyone who touches you gets a mild physical consequence, or 1 physical stress if they don’t have the open slot. This effect lasts until the end of the scene, but you can end it at will.

entities.name: Temperature Reduction
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can create freezer-cold temperatures at will, rendering your zone or an adjacent zone uncomfortably chilly.

entities.name: Ice Slick
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

As an action, you can create a patch of ice that fills your zone or an adjacent zone. You can move through the ice easily, but to friends and foes it is a Fair (+2) obstacle. The slick lasts until the beginning of your next turn.

entities.name: Slowing
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can encase your opponents in ice, stopping them in their tracks.

entities.name: Ice Shield
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can encase yourself in a thin shell of ice, giving you Armor:4 against the next attack you suffer, at which point the bonus ends. Moving or taking a physical action breaks the shell, ending this bonus.

entities.name: Blizzard
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can dial down the temperature so quickly that snow forms in your zone and every adjacent zone. You can move through the snow without a problem, but to everyone else it’s a Fair (+2) obstacle that persists until the end of the scene.

entities.name: Dark Sight
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You are built for the shadows. You can see perfectly well in any lighting, down to and including pitch blackness.

entities.name: Shadow Dodge
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

While you’re hiding in the shadows, you gain +2 to defend against ranged attacks.

entities.name: Dark Aura
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your very presence sucks the light out of rooms. Once per scene, you can create a situation aspect to reflect this, such as Darkened Room or Deep Shadows.

entities.name: Invisibility
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can wrap yourself in the shadows even in the brightest room.

entities.name: Teleportation
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Shadows are connected in a metaphysical way even you can’t quite understand. But you can use this fact to step into one shadow and out of a distant one.

entities.name: Shadow Beast
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can summon a creature made out of darkness itself into your zone. This shadow beast has Great (+4) Physique, Fight, and Athletics, as well as the aspects Made of Shadows and Bestial Fury. The beast is an NPC who will attack nearby targets at random, although characters can use Provoke to get it going after a particular target. It will not attack you; however, there’s nothing preventing it from attacking your allies. The beast will dissolve away at the end of the scene or when you dismiss it.

entities.name: Growth
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use your super form to grow massive! While in this form, you are at least twice your normal height, and you gain +1 to all attack rolls because of your overwhelming power.

entities.name: Shrinking
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can use your super form to become tiny! While in this form, you’re a quarter of your normal size or less, and you gain +1 to all defense rolls because you’re so hard to hit.

entities.name: Cocoon
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

In addition to your standard super-form, you can use your ability to encase yourself in a protective shell. While in the shell you cannot move or take actions, but you have Armor:8 against all physical damage. You can only hold onto this form for a few minutes at a time.

entities.name: Hyper-Mode
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You are hiding an even more powerful transformation, one so powerful that the very act of transformation does damage to your environment, and which you can only hold on to for a few minutes at a time. While in hyper-mode, you can use special effects whenever you tie or succeed on a roll while using your power, in addition to when you succeed with style.

entities.name: Intense Training
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Choose one skill from Athletics, Fight, Shoot, or Physique. You may add special effects to any use of this skill as if it were a part of your power suite.

entities.name: Nice Toys
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Your incredible tech had to come from somewhere. You gain +2 to Contacts when dealing with people who either built your tech or work in the appropriate industry.

entities.name: Shiny Shiny
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

Sometimes just showing off your fancy equipment gets folks on your side. You can use Resources, with a +2 bonus, in place of Rapport when showing off the quality of your tech to someone would work to your advantage.

entities.name: Take Up Arms
entities.description:
*From the Venture City SRD.*

You can pass off your equipment to someone else. By doing so, they can use your power in addition to their own, but you will be powerless for the duration. Of course, being unfamiliar and untrained with your equipment, they’ll likely cause a lot of collateral damage just trying to use it.

entities.name: Keen Senses
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When you invoke aspects on a Notice roll, you can invoke any number of aspects, provided you have the fate points to cover the cost.

entities.name: Ally’s Shield
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can invoke Dwarven Shield-Maiden when a nearby ally suffers an attack. When you do, redirect that attack to yourself. Your defense is Average (+1) against that attack.

entities.name: Berserk Rage
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When you suffer a physical consequence, you can invoke that consequence for free on your next attack. If you suffer multiple physical consequences, you get a free invocation for each.

entities.name: Charge Like Ox
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Because you are Strong Like Ox, once per scene, as a single action, you may move two zones in a straight line then make a physical attack.

entities.name: Teflon Troublemaker
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When your Can’t Keep His Big Mouth Shut aspect is compelled to make you the target of an attack, you may immediately clear any mild consequences you currently have, instead of taking a fate point.

entities.name: A Friend in Every Port
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Whenever you enter a settlement, you may declare you’ve visited it before and roll Contacts against Fair (+2) opposition. If you succeed, you have a friend there who owes you one favor—nothing costly or life threatening. If you succeed with style, your friend will do any one thing for you that is within his power.

entities.name: Whirlwind Step
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When you assume the stance of the whirlwind, roll Athletics against Fair (+2) opposition. If you succeed, you may run on vertical surfaces and leap unlikely distances without making rolls to do so, until your next turn ends. If you succeed with style, you may instead gain these benefits for the rest of the scene.

entities.name: Backstab
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When you can surprise an enemy or attack from a place of hiding, you can attack with Stealth. If you succeed, you create a boost. If you succeed with style, you get to invoke that boost for free twice.

entities.name: Cover
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You have a cover identity you can assume. Describe your cover identity, choose a high concept and a trouble aspect for your cover identity, and choose an apex skill for your cover identity. You can assume that identity with enough preparation and the expenditure of a fate point. While you’re in that identity, its high concept and trouble replace yours and you can use Deceive in place of its apex skill. You lose these benefits as soon as your cover is blown, and you may have to spend some time creating a new cover identity.

entities.name: Criminal Underbelly
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Whenever you enter a settlement for the first time, you can spend a fate point to declare that the local criminals know you. Choose one of the following: they have a lead on a promising job, they’ll give you and your companions free room and board for a few weeks, or they’ll help you with something right now but you might owe them afterward.

entities.name: Elven High Magic
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can use Elf to cast spells relating to nature or growth, even if you have no other magical ability.

entities.name: Perfection in Battle
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Choose Shoot or Fight. When you’re using the traditional armaments of your people, you can use Elf instead of the chosen skill.

entities.name: Thick Skin
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may use Orc instead of Physique to determine your physical stress and consequences, and you get one additional minor physical consequence.

entities.name: One-Shift Boxes
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Every stress box absorbs only one shift of harm, but check as many as you want at a time. This option makes characters significantly more fragile.

entities.name: Check Two
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Check up to two boxes at once, add their values together, and reduce the hit by that many shifts. This option makes characters significantly tougher—a character with five stress boxes can take up to 9 shifts of harm in a scene without resorting to a consequence.

entities.name: Step Down
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Stress goes away gradually rather than all at once. Instead of clearing a stress box automatically at the end of a scene, erase it and check the box to its left (assuming there is one).

entities.name: Bonus Only
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Characters have zero stress boxes to start, but still get bonus boxes from skills like Physique and Will. This makes characters more fragile and emphasizes consequences.

entities.name: Extra Effort
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Voluntarily check a box anytime for a bonus on a roll. The bonus equals the value of the checked box. This can have unpredictable effects on your game. Not only can it result in some swingy rolls, it can also partially supplant the usual fate point economy. When combined with any of the above options, though, it becomes a little more viable.

entities.name: Stress-Free
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Characters have no stress boxes and don’t receive bonus boxes from skills. Instead, those skills grant one bonus mild consequence (physical or mental) at Good (+3) or two at Great (+4). This is the most dangerous and dynamic option—every hit results in a consequence and has narrative impact—but can potentially mean an unmanageable number of aspects in play.

entities.name: Extreme Effort
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Voluntarily take a consequence anytime for a bonus on a roll equal to the consequence’s value—mild grants +2, moderate +4, or severe +6. This can be dangerous, both to the PC and to the fate point economy, as with Extra Effort, above.

entities.name: Group Consequences
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Instead of tracking them individually, supporting and main NPCs share a pool of group consequences. This gives you the option to “sacrifice” a supporting NPC now to make a main NPC more challenging later. For every two supporting NPCs you expect to include in the scenario, add two mild and one moderate group consequences, to a maximum of three moderate group consequences. For each main NPC, add another mild, moderate, and severe group consequence. If a supporting or main NPC concedes, base the concession reward on the total number of consequences that NPC used during that scene.

entities.name: Collateral Consequences
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

In addition to their usual complement of consequences, the players can also make use of three communal consequences, one of each degree of severity. These represent damage to the environment or new complications in the story, such as Injured Bystanders or Anti-Mutant Hysteria. Players can effectively use them to offload harm from themselves onto the world around them. A collateral consequence can be cleared just like a regular one, using an overcome action with whatever skill seems most appropriate, with two exceptions. One, it must be done during the scene in which the consequence is incurred. Two, there’s no delay—with a good enough skill roll it clears immediately. This option is best suited for genres, such as supers, in which the PCs are likely to care a great deal about the world around them.

entities.name: Chain Lighting
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Bolts arc from target to target with precision. For each -1 you take, you may add an additional target to the attack. Range penalty is determined by the most distant target, -1 per zone from the starting zone.

entities.name: Thunderbolt
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When hitting a single target, thunder claps as lightning strikes. If you gain a boost on your attack, you generate an extra boost of Stunned.

entities.name: The Pieces of the Puzzle
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

When you take a few minutes to study a particular item and its position, you can reasonably reconstruct the chain of events that led to it being there. This reconstruction will be accurate, though it will not reveal any more than the necessary details. For example, it might reveal that it was carried by hand at some point, but not by whom.

entities.name: The Vault of the Eye
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may look at a scene and recall it in perfect detail. In practice, this allows you to ask the GM questions about that memory long after the fact, and take your time performing Investigation rolls. This includes anything you might ask about if you were still in the same place and time, such as the contents of containers. If the answer to the question would require a skill roll—such as picking a lock to see a chest’s contents—you may try normally, as if you were still there.

entities.name: The Blessing of a Thousand Tongues
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may learn any language quickly. With tutelage, it takes only a day. With only the opportunity to read or listen, it takes a week. If the source material is especially sparse, it may take as long as a month.

entities.name: The Eye Sees All Paths
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may not know everything, but you always know how to find out. When looking for a fairly specific piece of information, you may give the GM a fate point to be told the closest place you can go to find out, no matter how obscure or lost the information is. In short, you can never hit a wall when trying to find something out.

entities.name: Stars Illuminate the Night
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

So long as there is the faintest amount of light, you can see as if it were a bright day. In the rare case of utter darkness, you can see as well as if you had a light source.

entities.name: Giant’s Appetite
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can eat anything without harm. Not just foodstuffs—if you can chew and swallow it, or drink it, you can safely consume it, and even gain sustenance from it. You may casually ignore poisons, decay, shards of glass, and similar inconveniences. As a bonus, flavors are very distinctive and memorable to you, which allows for disgusting tricks like comparing the taste of blood samples to see if they’re from the same source, as well as more useful tricks like identifying a familiar poison.

entities.name: None May Bind The Giant
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

If you are restrained or shackled, you may break those bonds, so long as they are natural or manufactured. No door or lock may withstand more than a single blow from you. Barriers with no opening take longer, but you are effectively an entire sapping team with nothing more than fists and feet and anything else you can bring to bear.

entities.name: The Mind Is the Greatest Mountain
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

So far as social skills are concerned, you do not exist. You cannot be swayed, befriended, intimidated, or otherwise moved. Your speech reveals nothing about you or the veracity of your words. For purposes of the Villager’s ability, your Deceive score is higher than the Villager’s Empathy.

entities.name: Never Broken
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You gain a -8 physical consequence which recovers in the same way a -2 consequence does.

entities.name: The Accounting of Small Things
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Once you have successfully stolen something small enough to fit in a pocket, it is gone until you choose to reveal it again. No amount of searching—or even stripping—will reveal the purloined item. You may only have one such item at a time hidden in this fashion.

entities.name: The Supplication of Locks
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You need only whisper your name into a lock to attempt to pick it, as if using a full set of tools. If successful, the attempt takes only a moment. If unsuccessful, you may try again the old-fashioned way.

entities.name: Corroboration of Coincidence
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Fate favors your lies with minor coincidences and circumstantial evidence that seem to lend them credence. You may apply a boost to the scene before you roll Deceive, so long as you can describe how it helps you look more honest. If successful, the boost turns into an aspect on the scene.

entities.name: Stealing Words from the Wind
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You make no noise you do not wish to be heard. Not only does this allow you to move in absolute silence, but you can also use it selectively, such as speaking so only one person can hear you.

entities.name: Spears of Green Wood
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may train a body of troops—unnamed characters in a group of up to approximately 100—for a week and increase their Fight Skill by +1. You can repeat this multiple times, improving any given unit to a maximum of your Fight -2.

entities.name: To the Horizon
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Anything you can see is effectively one zone from you when you shoot.

entities.name: To the Stars
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Any missile fired into the air can land any place you know or near anyone you can name. Messages and small items can be delivered in this fashion. This cannot be used to launch an attack directly, but if fired with ill intent, it is entirely possible to kill a horse or unnamed NPC nearby.

entities.name: Crown of Menace
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You are too terrifying to be attacked. Until you make a physical attack in a scene, characters with a Will lower than Good (+3) simply cannot attack you. Those with sufficient Will to attack still flinch on their first attack, though, automatically missing.

entities.name: All Things in Their Place
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You always know the power dynamic in the room, and you may insert yourself within it anywhere you desire. Use this with caution—while it impacts how people interact with you, it does not equate to actual authority, and placing yourself too highly—especially over people not used to being anything but top dog—can inspire an unpleasant response.

entities.name: War of Papers
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can take action against organizations through indirect measures. Effectively you can fight on the level of any organization smaller than a nation without the need to recruit allies or have any organization of your own. Yes, this means you can effectively “kill” a city, or even an army, given enough time.

entities.name: The Conjunction of Form
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may combine materials in impossible ways, giving one the attribute of another. You may make paper with the strength of steel, or steel with the weight of paper. Doing so requires the two aspects—one for the material, one for the additional attribute—to be invoked simultaneously on the Crafts roll to create the finished product.

entities.name: Architecture of the Heart
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Reading a room is a triviality to you. Even more, you can spot the emotional lynchpins in a room and easily understand how actions would impact the mood. If you roll Empathy to read a room—difficulty Mediocre (+0)—count how many shifts you accrue. Over the course of the scene, you may ask the GM to tell you how people would react to any hypothetical scenario. You can do this a number of times equal to the number of shifts generated.

entities.name: The Inner Eye Sees Inner Truth
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Without rolling, you can tell if another character is lying so long as the target’s Deceive is equal to or lower than your Empathy. In the case of high Deceive, you will know that you cannot tell, but will never receive a “false positive.”

entities.name: By Rote
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may pick three spells that you know well enough that you don’t need to consult your notes to cast.

entities.name: Evil Eye
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can attempt to put Bad Luck on a target with nothing more than an obvious gesture. This lasts only a day.

entities.name: Interior Decorator
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You may call it feng shui on your invoices, but it’s all just decor. If you put a spell on a place, you may arrange the furniture and decorations just so. If you do, the effect lasts for up to a season—or until someone rearranges the furnishings.

entities.name: Ironskin
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Unarmed blows now strike like a metal weapon, and the character may add +2 per MP spent to any feat of pure strength.

entities.name: The Drunkard’s Stagger
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You sway and stagger on your feet, evading enemy blows seemingly by chance. When you succeed in a defensive Athletics roll using this technique, you gain +1 on your next attack against the opponent who tried to hit you. If you succeed with style, gain +2.

entities.name: The Drunken Shove
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Your rude and artless push contains a greater power than seems possible. You gain +2 to use Physique to create an advantage on an opponent by knocking them off balance.

entities.name: Drinking from the Jug
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You pause to take a swig of wine from your jug, fortifying yourself for the battle. When you have a drink during a fight, clear your lowest stress box. This requires you to take an entire action drinking.

entities.name: Pouring Wine
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

(Requires Drinking from the Jug) You take out a cup and pour a drink from your jug. This elaborate and difficult task causes a pause in the battle. No one may attack you while you pour, and you remove your lowest stress mark. This technique requires an entire action, and you may not perform the technique more than once in a row.

entities.name: Steady the Drunkard
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

(Requires Drunkard Swings Wide) You stagger and seem about to fall, so you reach out and grab your opponent’s arm to steady yourself. This seemingly unintentional grip blocks chi and paralyzes your opponent. You may place a Chi Blocked situation aspect with a free invocation on your opponent. Your opponent may not use any kung fu stunts until they remove this aspect.

entities.name: Cyber-Heart
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can install and use other cyber-augs. The heart also acts as a backup for your natural heart and filters impurities and toxins from your blood. If you’re subject to a poison or toxin, spend a fate point to ignore it. If you’re ever killed by something the cyber-heart could conceivably save you from, spend a fate point to concede instead of being taken out.

entities.name: Trick Shots
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

+2 to create an advantage with Shoot when you use the grapnel gun to swing around, disarm an opponent, or create a barrier.

entities.name: Pierce the Veil of Lies
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Spend a fate point. Three times during the scene, you can ask the GM if someone is lying, and she must answer you truthfully.

entities.name: Hard to Pin Down
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Take a +2 on any Overcome roll made to retreat from a combat zone.

entities.name: Blitzkrieg
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Your squad is fast, light, and deadly. Take +2 on all Operation rolls in which your attack focuses on catching the enemy off-guard.

entities.name: Hi-Tech Gear
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can use Equipment instead of Operations in any situation where raw technological superiority would win the day.

entities.name: Well-Stocked
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You gain a +2 on all Equipment rolls made to create an advantage when you are accessing your preexisting supplies.

entities.name: Codebreakers
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

On a successful Recon roll to create an advantage while monitoring enemy communications, you can discover or create one additional aspect (though this doesn’t give you an extra free invocation).

entities.name: Counterprogramming
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

You can use Recon instead of Operations to set a trap when you use the enemy’s communications system against them.

entities.name: Scouting
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

A unit can use Notice to put a new zone aspect in play in an adjacent zone that doesn’t already have a unit in it. The difficulty is Fair (+2), +2 for each aspect the zone already has. For example, if a zone has the aspect Tangled Woods, the difficulty to give it a second aspect would be Great (+4).

entities.name: Surrounded
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

A unit can put a Surrounded into play if it has more allies than enemies in its zone. Each allied unit in the zone gets a +1 to its attacks as long as this aspect remains in play.

entities.name: Compels Aplenty
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

While compels aren’t tools for forcing outcomes, they are tools for making things go wrong. So make them abundant. Place aspects on the scene, the story, the campaign—and compel them to make things go wrong for everyone. Simply dropping Death Comes for Everyone onto the story and compelling it at the exact worst time (for the players) to make things that much worse will get lots of traction. Yeah, the players affected will walk away with some fate points—which they’ll need in order to survive—but they’ll also feel the emotional gut-punch of the moment—and will wonder when the next compel is going to land. Make them hurt. Make them worry.

entities.name: Every Path a Dark One
entities.description:
*From the Fate System Toolkit SRD.*

Aspects aren’t the only way to evoke atmosphere. You can deliver, too, with obstacles and zones. It’s never easy to run away from horror, so clutter the path to salvation with obstacles. (Read more on obstacles, below.) And when you’re drawing your zone maps, make it all more claustrophobic than usual: more zones covering less space. While the physical distances aren’t any different, it’s just plain harder to get away from the dangerous places in horror—in a regular house, the front door might just be a zone away. In a haunted house? Try more like five or ten… and never let them sprint the full length.

entities.name: I’ve Drunk Worse
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

You’ve grown accustomed to toxic fumes and chemical burns. You can use Alchemy to defend against attacks and aspects involving poisons, toxins, and other chemicals.

entities.name: Doctor
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Your alchemical studies include treating the ailments of the human body. You can roll Alchemy to allow another character to begin recovering physical consequences. Characters who have Alchemy at Average (+1) or higher can provide you with teamwork bonuses on recovery rolls, even if they don’t have the Doctor stunt.

entities.name: Superior Tactics
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

When it comes to naval battles, you’ve seen every trick in the book. +2 when actively opposing Sail rolls to create positional aspects.

entities.name: Second Star to the Right
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Charts and arithmetic mills will never replace the instincts of a good navigator. +2 to Sail overcome rolls to improve the speed of a journey.

entities.name: Freefall Wrestling
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

While in zero gravity, you can use Athletics instead of Fight to make unarmed, hand-to-hand attacks against an opponent.

entities.name: A Finely Tuned Machine
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

When you stack an advantage by invoking one of your engineering-related aspects, and give it to an ally using your ship’s equipment to perform an action, you grant that ally a +3 bonus instead of the usual +2.

entities.name: Miracle Worker
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Once per session, after you succeed on a Crafts roll to begin recovering a ship’s consequence when outside combat, you can spend a fate point to immediately remove the consequence.

entities.name: Subtle Signaling
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

By understanding the relationship between lantern signals and the hexagrams of the I Ching, you can construct signals that carry hidden significance. To understand the hidden message, an observer must have the Subtle Signaling stunt or must successfully overcome with Lore, opposed by your Deceive.

entities.name: The Finest Snake Oil
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

You’ve learned enough scientific jargon to convince people that the flasks of colored vinegar you’re selling are elixirs of youth or miracle cure-alls. +2 to Deceive while trying to convince someone that you’ve produced a remarkable feat of alchemy.

entities.name: Eightfold Formation
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

From your study of battle formations, you know how to arrange your troops for any situation. During crew combat, you can use Lore instead of Will to benefit units under your command. See the Fate System Toolkit (page 167) for a list of these benefits.

entities.name: Empty Fort Strategy
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Your knowledge of armies and warfare allows you to construct a convincing illusion on the battlefield. You can use Lore instead of Deceive to create a plausible but untrue situation aspect on a zone. Creating this aspect requires enough time before the enemy arrives to arrange the scene appropriately—creating false tracks, propping up rifles in windows, and so forth.

entities.name: We Have Already Won
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Before a physical conflict begins, if you have advance knowledge of the area in which the battle will take place, and you have the opportunity to discuss tactics with allies, you can use Notice to create an aspect on a single zone without actually being there. This aspect represents the benefits of planning and scouting, such as Coordinated Ambush or We’ll Hold Them At This Pass. You can use this stunt for crew battles and for conflicts between individual characters.

entities.name: Iron Grip
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Your crew is too afraid of you to keep any secrets from you. You can use Provoke instead of Empathy to detect changes in the crew’s mood or to discover any secrets or plots the crew is hiding from you.

entities.name: Hit Them Where It Hurts
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

When you successfully attack a ship, you choose—rather than the defender—whether the ship must absorb the attack with ship consequences or crew conditions. The target chooses which specific consequences or conditions to use.

entities.name: Warning Shots
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

a well-timed volley of cannon fire can discourage enemy ships. Once per exchange, you can use Shoot to oppose an enemy ship’s attempt to create a position aspect against any ship.

entities.name: Master and Commander
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Once per scene, when your crew or battle unit performs a single action under your command, you can substitute your Will for any skill the crew or unit would have used. This Will roll cannot be improved with teamwork bonuses.

entities.name: One With the Ship
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Your sweat and blood keeps the ship going in the worst circumstances. When the ship would take a consequence, your character can instead choose to take an equivalent consequence.

entities.name: Fine Sails
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

High-quality materials provide better resistance to the winds, which produces higher maximum speed. The ship’s navigator gains +2 to Sail when determining travel times or racing other vessels.

entities.name: Maneuverable
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

The mechanisms operating the ship’s sails have been improved. The crew gains +2 to Sail rolls to gain or remove positional aspects during combat.

entities.name: Long Guns
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Lengthened barrels and expanded prometheum chambers extend the range of the ship’s guns. As long as the ship can maintain an At Long Range aspect between itself and its opponent, it gains an ongoing +2 to defend against attacks from that opponent. The At Long Range aspect can still be invoked as normal.

entities.name: Chain Shot
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Firing lengths of chain from the ship’s guns gives a better chance of inflicting serious damage to enemy sails. The ship gains +2 to Shoot when attempting to create a negative aspect on a target representing damaged sails.

entities.name: False Hull
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Cleverly built into the ship’s structure, this hidden space can store a small amount of cargo, less than 5% of the ship’s total cargo tonnage. Add +2 to the opposition to any attempts to find the hidden cargo.

entities.name: Ramming Prow
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

A reinforced, sharply pointed prow allows the ship to deliver a ramming attack while minimizing harm to itself. When delivering a ramming attack, the ship receives +2 to defend itself against the damage from this attack. See Ship Combat for more information on this.

entities.name: Repairs
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

The ship’s crew can roll Craft to attempt to remove damage-related aspects from the ship. During a conflict, the crew cannot attempt to recover damage-related consequences, but they can create aspects to represent temporary repairs, such as Held Together with Twine and Hope or We Didn’t Need That Gear Anyway. Any character on the ship can invoke a temporary repair aspect in response to an opponent invoking a consequence on the ship.

entities.name: Signaling
entities.description:
*From the Sails Full of Stars SRD.*

Once per exchange, a ship can transmit a single message using its signaling lanterns. To judge whether a message can be sent during a single exchange, assume that signaling speed is roughly similar to that of Morse code—about forty words per minute. Normally, signaling does not require a roll, but it does use the signaling character’s action for the exchange.

entities.name: All For One
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I take the openings my friends give me, once per conflict I get +2 to my next attack after an ally takes out an enemy.

entities.name: Former Gendarme
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I was once a gendarme, I get +1 to create an advantage or overcome when I get help from my former colleagues.

entities.name: Genius
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am the smartest person in the room, I get +2 to overcome puzzles and traps.

entities.name: Giant
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am a giant of a person, I get +2 to overcome actions when I break things.

entities.name: Idealistic
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am idealistic, I gain +2 to defend against intimidation and threats.

entities.name: Master of Disguise
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am a master of disguise with a knack for being in the right place at the right time, once per session I can join a scene already in progress, having posed as a minor character.

entities.name: Pub Legend
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am a legend in bars across the world, I get +2 to create an advantage by gathering information in the pub.

entities.name: Racing Sloop
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I have a fast, sleek, racing ship, I gain +2 to overcome actions when I put the pedal to the metal in racing contests.

entities.name: Rocket Racer
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Because I am a master pilot I get +2 to overcome in chases when I fly through narrow or twisting spaces.

entities.name: Acrobatic
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to create an advantage when using obstacles, furniture, or terrain for superior positioning.

entities.name: Flashy
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to create an advantage when intimidating an opponent with a demonstration of your style.

entities.name: Quick
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 when determining turn order.

entities.name: Steady
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

When you succeed with style creating an advantage, gain +1 to your next defense roll.

entities.name: Subtle
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Invoking your fencing aspect to create an advantage based on misdirection grants +3 instead of +2.

entities.name: Impenetrable
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Increase your Armor value by +1.

entities.name: Perfect Footwork
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

When you succeed with style on defense, you may create a situation aspect with a free invocation instead of gaining a boost.

entities.name: Powerful
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

When you tie on attack you create a situation aspect with one free invoke instead of gaining a boost.

entities.name: Precise
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Increase the Weapon rating of your main hand by +1.

entities.name: Cutlass
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to create an advantage when you try to disarm your opponent.

entities.name: Rapier
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Invoking your Swordplay aspect for a bonus on an attack grants a +3 instead of +2.

entities.name: Saber
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

When you invoke a situation aspect about your fencing style that you created as an obstacle, increase the opposition by an additional +1.

entities.name: Small Sword
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to attack an enemy who has already acted in the round.

entities.name: Buckler
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to your next attack when you succeed on defense.

entities.name: Cloak
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to create an advantage when you obfuscate your weapon.

entities.name: Empty
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

Gain +1 to attack when you swing with both hands.

entities.name: Main Gauche
entities.description:
*From the Three Rocketeers: No-Skill Swashbuckling SRD.*

When you succeed with style on defense against an attack you may deal a 2-shift physical hit with your off hand instead of gaining a boost.

entities.name: Grenadier
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

By spending a fate point, you can physically attack everyone in a zone.

entities.name: Bodyguard
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Designate a character, place, or object to guard. Whenever that thing is attacked and you are in the same zone, you can spend a fate point to redirect the attack to yourself. You gain Armor:1 against this attack.

entities.name: Naysayer
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

+2 to create advantages with Provoke by fomenting arguments that undermine the PCs or make them look foolish.

entities.name: Sniper
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

When you attack with Shoot and invoke an aspect representing careful aim, you gain Weapon:2 on the attack.

entities.name: Sneak Attack
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Provided you haven’t been spotted by your target yet, you can attack with Sneak instead of Fight.

entities.name: Ninja Vanish (Fate Adversary Toolkit)
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

By spending a fate point, you can make yourself vanish from the scene entirely. Then, at the end of any later turn, you can spend another fate point to make yourself reappear anywhere in the scene and immediately attack.

entities.name: Connected
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Once per session, you can draw on your contacts to bring in reinforcements. These reinforcements take the form of either one hitter with an apex skill rated equal to your Contacts, two threats with apex skills rated one step lower than your Contacts, or Fair (+2) fillers equal in number to your Contacts. When you use this stunt, you can spend one fate point to gain +2 to Contacts, to a maximum of Great (+4), for the purpose of bringing in these reinforcements.

entities.name: Escape Plan (Fate Adversary Toolkit)
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Once per session, if you would get taken out, you can spend a fate point to concede instead.

entities.name: Mook Shield
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Whenever you are attacked, you can spend a fate point to divert the attack to nearby filler enemies.

entities.name: Scout Armor
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

The scout has Armor:1 against small-arms fire and melee weapons.

entities.name: Contingency Plan
entities.description:
*From the Fate Adversary Toolkit SRD.*

Whenever Baron von Darkness takes a consequence, you can pay a fate point to remove him from the scene (in a puff of smoke), replacing him with two threats.

entities.name: Friends in High Places
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

+2 to overcome with Rapport when socializing at a fancy gathering, such as a ritzy corporate or government function.

entities.name: Expert Marksman
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

+1 to attack or create an advantage with Combat when using a firearm.

entities.name: Martial Artist
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

+1 to create an advantage with Combat or Athletics when fighting unarmed.

entities.name: Backstab (Atomic Robo)
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

Use Stealth instead of Combat to attack when the target isn’t aware of you.

entities.name: Riposte
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

When you use Combat to defend in melee and succeed with style, spend a fate point to immediately inflict an attack on your opponent at the shift value of your defense. For example, if you get four shifts on your defense, you’d deal a 4-shift hit to the attacker. You can’t do this again until you have another “next action” to spend (after your skipped turn goes by).

entities.name: Mind Over Matter
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

Once per scene, you may check a mental stress box to absorb physical harm.

entities.name: Knuckledusters
entities.description:
*From the Atomic Robo SRD.*

+1 to Combat to attack when unarmed, Weapon:2

entities.name: Ray Gun
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

Using your ray gun, you get +2 to Shoot attacks against targets at least one zone away.

entities.name: Sonic Excavator
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

Using your sonic excavator, you can carve a path through inanimate material with Science.

entities.name: Aircar
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

Using your aircar, you can fly very quickly at tree-top height. You can transport up to four other people and a small amount of cargo, but can’t fly with anything really heavy.

entities.name: Autodoc
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

When using your autodoc to treat wounds or disease with Science, once per session you can improve the outcome by one step: failure to tie, tie to success, or success to success with style. If you initially succeeded with style, you can create an aspect with one free invocation instead of gaining a boost.

entities.name: Handheld Expert System
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

Once per session, you can use your handheld expert system to automatically succeed on creating an advantage with Science against passive opposition equal to or less than your Science rank.

entities.name: Poltergeist
entities.description:
*From the Frontier Spirit SRD.*

The facet can interact with material objects using Physique during a scene where each of the facet’s portfolio aspects is embodied by an aspect on anything in the scene. It can attack or create advantages, but cannot be attacked. This costs one fate point per exchange, and the manifestation ends if any of the requisite aspects are removed.
